Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked great. Procurement/Legal reviewed the DPA you sent and attached a redline (Litmus_DPA_redline_20260214.docx). Two questions popped up that are blocking signature:

1) EU transfers — Litmus requires either documented SCCs or evidence that data flow is restricted to EU regions. Our legal team flagged the transfer clause and asked whether Redwood can commit to SCCs or provide a suitable transfer mechanism.

2) KMS requirement — because we will process regulated PII, our security team asks if we can support customer-managed keys or at least provide a KMS attestation.

Can you route these to security/legal for a quick take? Procurement wants to know if this will need an exception request or if it can be handled in the DPA itself. We’re hoping to close this by month-end.

Thanks,
Daniel

Subject: RE: DPA redline + EU transfer and KMS question

Folks — quick read of the redline: Litmus removed our standard EU transfer paragraph and substituted language that would require us to sign onto their on-prem-style obligations. We can accept SCCs in principle, but the redline as written is incompatible.

About KMS: Redwood does not currently support customer-managed HSM keys in Hosted mode. We do offer a KMS attestation and can provide SOC2 evidence. If Litmus insists on CMK/HSM we’d need a Private deployment / dedicated contract and an exception approval (security + commercial) — that typically adds 6–8 weeks.

Recommended next steps:
- Offer SCCs + provide SOC2/KMS attestation (fast path).
- If client demands CMK, escalate to Security leadership for exception; confirm additional cost/schedule.

Rishi — can you confirm whether we have any precedents for a time-boxed exception approval to meet a month-end close?

Priyom
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:31:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: DPA redline + EU transfer and KMS question

Short answer: we can fast-track an exception review but it’s not a guaranteed approval. Steps: security assessment (2–3 business days), risk committee review (1 week), executive sign-off if risk > medium (3–5 business days). If Litmus will accept SCCs + attestation, that’s the least friction and we can sign within 48 hours after doc update.

Naomi — can you draft the attestation language (privacy + KMS limitations) so I can include it in the counter?

Rishi
Head of Risk & Compliance

Attestation draft attached. My notes:
- We will provide a KMS attestation stating that keys for hosted customers are managed by Redwood using industry standard KMS (GCP/KMS or AWS KMS depending on region) and we do not presently support customer-provided keys for hosted tenants.
